scores.title: P1 CNX-EV2 at 224: ConvNeXt-Tiny + EfficientNetV2-S, modern recipe, EMA, D4 TTA, equal-weight ensemble, val-selected logit adjustment
scores.comment: Total = unweighted mean. Two CNN members only; both refuters put the ensemble at ~86.0-86.3 (P(>=87) 0.25-0.35) and the EfficientNetV2-S member is the least supported (trained at 300/384 px, SAME-padding emulation, 0.86x ConvNeXt speed, 76.38 under MedMNIST+). Budget does not close: 50 epochs, 3 seeds and 4 ablations need ~280-330 GPU-min over three sessions, the CPU DataLoader path is unmeasured on 2 vCPUs, and the torchvision-v2 TrivialAugment subclass crashes (_augmentation_space does not exist in v2). Strongest points, all adopted: pre-registered final-EMA weights, saved per-view logits, medmnist Evaluator, DermaMNIST-E external test, McNemar vs PRIME-B, three-arm recipe ablation (from the fixes).

scores.title: P2 DINOv2-first at native 224 px: LLRD-fine-tuned ViT-S/14 + ViT-B/14 + DenseNet-121, frozen LP/kNN guardrail, D4 TTA, pre-registered equal-weight ensemble, frozen decision_rule.json
scores.comment: Highest ceiling: every >85 number in the literature (audited or not) at 224 px is a ViT, and the one peer-reviewed single-seed source with saved probabilities (Sanap 2026) has ViT-B at 90.57. Refuters correctly cut the point estimate (87.5 -> ~86.3-86.5 pre-signal; DINOv2-B LP is 83.97 < DINO 84.87, so Anchor 1 is wrong; ViT-B/14 throughput 55-70 img/s not 80-90; EMA warm-up semantics; Mixup even-batch assert; DenseNet row is not a reproduction as written). Fits a T4 (Session 1 ~110-120 min). Best protocol discipline of the three (decision rule frozen before test, LP guardrail, temperature scaling, DenseNet anchor). It is essentially what the running Phase-3 scaffold already implements, so it is the natural skeleton of the merged plan.

scores.title: P3 L-PRIME: lesion-aware balanced-softmax 4-member ensemble + distillation + calibration + conformal, lesion identity recovered for the official split
scores.comment: Balanced softmax (tau_train=1) costs 0.3-0.8 top-1 at the natural prior, 1/m_lesion sampling de-weights exactly the leaked multi-image lesions (honest but lowers the official number), point B is <= point A by construction, and the distilled student is over-claimed (LS teachers + fixed-view logits: Beyer et al., Muller et al.). Six ConvNeXt-T trainings plus a student, ~260-280 GPU-min over three sessions, with concrete bugs (ViT-S/14 at 128/176 px crashes, torch.quantile 2^24 limit, densenet121.tv_in1k is not the MedMNIST+ anchor, A5 is the MedMNIST v2 not MedMNIST+ protocol, kornia black corners). Its single best idea, recovering lesion_id for every official image with hard validation gates and reporting a lesion-clean test subset, is the most reviewer-proof contribution of the whole programme and is adopted as a primary analysis, together with the zero-shot DermaMNIST-E evaluation and the file/MD5 verification work.

winner: P2 DINOv2-first (skeleton), merged with P1's ConvNeXt-T member and pre-registration/artefact discipline and P3's lesion-identity audit, lesion-clean subset and DermaMNIST-E/-C handling
rationale: All six refutations converge on the same verdict: the plans are executable on a free T4, the protocols are sound, and the NUMBERS (87-87.5 point estimates) were unsupported by audited evidence (nothing peer-reviewed and multi-seed exceeds MedMNIST+ DenseNet-121 84.74 on this split). I accept that verdict for the pre-registration, but two facts in the project files that the refuters did not have change the frame rather than the protocol. (1) Session 1 is already running recipe v1 (prime3_colab.py, launched 13:46) and its ConvNeXt-T seed 0 reached 89.9% EMA validation top-1 at epoch 15/30; with 43% of validation images sharing a lesion with train, that implies ~84-86% on lesion-clean images and ~87.5-89.5% on the 38.8%-leaked test set for a single member, i.e. the regularised recipe memorises leaked lesions anyway and the refuters' anti-memorisation discount was too pessimistic. (2) The literature update (research/lit_sweep.json) shows the real 224-px bar is a memorisation regime (Sanap 2026: no augmentation, batch 4, val-accuracy early stopping, single seed: ViT-B 90.57, stacking 91.67; Wu & Papiez 92.02 unaudited), and Sanap publishes test softmax outputs, so for the first time a paired McNemar test and a clean-vs-leaked decomposition of a published system are possible. The paper's defensible contribution is therefore not a headline number but: a pre-registered, saved-probability, 3-seed result with CIs; a direct measurement of how much official-split accuracy is leaked-lesion memorisation (clean 1,227 vs leaked 778 images, regularised vs plain recipe, ours vs PRIME-B vs Sanap); and leakage-free DermaMNIST-E numbers. The merged plan keeps recipe v1 frozen (so Session 1's seed-0 runs are the primary members and no T4 time is wasted), fixes the one real bug (train_one saves no probabilities; a recovery cell rebuilds them from the saved fp16 EMA weights), drops EfficientNetV2-S from the primary (least supported, and timm's fine-grained layer decay leaves its stem at ~2e-8), uses 3 primary configurations x 3 seeds (ConvNeXt-T, DINOv2 ViT-B/14, DenseNet-121) plus DINOv2 ViT-S as ablation workhorse, adds the exact MedMNIST+ DenseNet-121 reproduction, a three-arm recipe/memorisation ladder, a resolution ladder, free inference-time ablations, and budgets four T4 sessions with a pre-declared cut order. P2 wins the scoring because it is the proposal the running scaffold already implements and has the best selection discipline; P1 contributes the ConvNeXt-T member and the artefact/pre-registration rules; P3 contributes the lesion audit and the -C/-E handling. Expected top-1 is stated as an interval, with the refuters' pre-signal estimate (~86) and the validation-informed update (ensemble 87.5-90.5, point 89.0, P(>=87) ~0.8, P(>=90) ~0.3) both recorded, so that whichever materialises is reported against a written expectation. No external services were contacted for this judgement; all file facts (MD5s, Zenodo file names, CSV headers, class counts) come from the refuters' and protocol author's verifications and from the local project files.
merged_plan:
MERGED PLAN -- "PRIME-3": pre-registered, leakage-audited 224-px DermaMNIST benchmark with a 3-member heterogeneous ensemble (ConvNeXt-T / DINOv2 ViT-B/14 / DenseNet-121), deterministic D4 TTA, validation-only operating points, and lesion-stratified + external (DermaMNIST-E) evaluation. Implemented as ONE training script for Colab (DDP_Phase2/phase3/prime3_colab.py v2, the running scaffold with the changes in section 11) plus ONE frozen CPU evaluation script (phase3/eval_phase3.py). Run-directory names stay as in the scaffold so phase3/aggregate_phase3.py keeps working.

0. IMMEDIATE ACTIONS (Session 1 has been running recipe v1 on the T4 since 13:46; ETA ~15:50)
0.1 BUG (confirmed by reading prime3_colab.py, which is byte-identical to session1_oneliner.txt): train_one() never np.save()s the member probabilities; only frozen_probe() does. At the end of Session 1 the ensemble stage computes runs == [] and crashes (np.mean([]) -> nan -> argmax error), and the results zip contains only results.json/PNG files. Each member's final EMA weights ARE written to /content/DDP_Phase3/<run>/model_final_fp16.pt (not zipped, not on Drive, lost when the runtime recycles). Do not interrupt the running cell. Prepare a RECOVERY cell now and run it the moment the main cell stops (the kernel namespace, X_VA/X_TE/set_norm/predict and /content survive the exception): (a) mount Drive; (b) for every /content/DDP_Phase3/*_s*/ with results.json but no test_tta_probs.npy: m = timm.create_model(cfg['model'], pretrained=False, num_classes=7, drop_path_rate as cfg, img_size=cfg['size'] if 'vit' in cfg['model']); load model_final_fp16.pt with every tensor cast to float32; .cuda().eval().to(memory_format=channels_last); set_norm(m); run the 8 dihedral views on X_VA, X_TE and (once section 2.3 is done) the -E test array; save val/test/extE_logits_views.npy (N,8,7) float32, *_tta_probs.npy (= mean over views of softmax; exactly the names the scaffold's ensemble stage expects), *_clean_probs.npy (view 0), y_val.npy, y_test.npy, y_extE.npy; (c) copy the whole /content/DDP_Phase3 tree INCLUDING the .pt files to Drive (ddp_phase3/runs/); (d) re-run the Session-1 cell: train_one()/frozen_probe() skip (results.json exists) and the ensemble stage now runs. Cost ~1 GPU-min per member. fp16-stored EMA weights reproduce the in-session fp32 probabilities to ~1e-3; state this in the paper.
0.2 FREEZE recipe v1 (= exactly the CONFIGS Session 1 is running; section 4) for every later seed and for the reference arm of every ablation. Session-1 seed-0 runs ARE the seed-0 primary members. Only artefact handling, evaluation and the new baseline/ablation configurations change. Reason: retraining seed 0 under a revised recipe costs one more free-tier day for recipe details (EMA horizon, black corners, EffNetV2 layer decay) that are disclosed, not wrong.
0.3 Write phase3/PREREGISTRATION.md now (time-stamped, committed to the GitHub repo) with sections 3-9 of this plan, before any Session-1 TEST metric is read. Session 1's cell prints per-member test metrics after each run; the paper discloses this and shows that every decision rule below is fixed independently of them.
0.4 From Session 2 on, the training loop prints validation metrics only; test probabilities are saved silently and read by eval_phase3.py alone (one invocation per seed-set, after decision_rule.json exists).

1. WHAT THE PAPER CLAIMS (frame)
Primary endpoint: top-1 ACC on the official DermaMNIST test split (2,005 images, dermamnist_224.npz), MedMNIST Evaluator definitions. Secondary: macro-AUC (MedMNIST getAUC = unweighted mean of 7 OvR AUCs), balanced ACC, macro-F1, top-3, melanoma AUROC and operating points, NLL/Brier/ECE. External: DermaMNIST-E test (1,511 ISIC-2018 images, lesion-disjoint from HAM10000). Structural: lesion-CLEAN (1,227) vs lesion-LEAKED (778) decomposition of the official test set for every system with per-image outputs, including Phase-2 PRIME-B and Sanap 2026. Claims: (i) the first pre-registered, saved-probability, multi-seed result on this split above the audited ceiling (84.74), if it is; (ii) a measured answer to how much official-split accuracy is leaked-lesion memorisation; (iii) leakage-free external numbers; (iv) validated operating points for balanced / melanoma-sensitive use. Never claim SOTA against unaudited preprints, 'clinically useful', or 'robust'.

2. DATA
2.1 Official MedMNIST+ files (Zenodo 10519652): dermamnist_224.npz (1,091,112,502 B, MD5 8974907d8e169bef5f5b96bc506ae45d), dermamnist_128.npz (MD5 2defd784463fa5243564e855ed717de1), dermamnist_64.npz (MD5 b70a2f5635c6199aeaa28c31d7202e1f); assert each MD5 against medmnist.INFO['dermamnist']['MD5_224'/'MD5_128'/'MD5_64'] and record it in config.json. Cache in Drive (ddp_phase3/data/), copy to /content at session start (~1 min; Zenodo direct download can take 2-15 min). Load uint8, keep NCHW uint8 on the GPU (1.5 GB), convert to float per batch (scaffold pattern); never a float32 copy of a split; never two 224-px files in RAM at once. Class order akiec 0, bcc 1, bkl 2, df 3, mel 4, nv 5, vasc 6; test counts 66/103/220/23/223/1341/29 (majority class 66.88%); val 33/52/110/12/111/671/14. Prior = the 7,007 train labels only. Assert test_labels_224 == test_labels_64 (same order as Phase 2) before any paired test.
2.2 Lesion identity for the official split: research/data/dermamnist_split_info.csv (split,index,image_id; index = 0-based position in each official array) + HAM10000_metadata.csv (lesion_id,image_id,dx,dx_type,age,sex,localization,dataset) + DermaMNIST-C.csv (Zenodo 12739457, CC BY 4.0). Hard gates, all of which must pass or the stratified analysis is dropped and the paper says so: dx mapped in MedMNIST order equals the npz labels for all 10,015 positions; cross-partition overlaps reproduce 886/641 (train-test), 440/332 (train-val), 128/113 (val-test), 51/40 (all three) and 1,006 multi-partition lesions; CLEAN test := official test image_ids that are in DermaMNIST-C's test split = exactly 1,227 images; LEAKED := the other 778 (773 share a lesion with train or val + 5 fastdup near-duplicates). Save phase3/results/test_lesion_map.csv (index,image_id,lesion_id,dx,dx_type,dataset,clean). Print per-class counts of CLEAN and LEAKED.
2.3 DermaMNIST-E (Zenodo 12739457): dermamnist_extended_224.npz (1,326,859,643 B, MD5 b59d6a78a036a0bb48a1eff13d94333c), cached in Drive. Load only f['test_images'] (1511,224,224,3), f['test_labels'] and f['train_labels'] (class-order gate: train counts must equal 327/514/1099/115/1113/6705/142). -E test prior differs (NV 60.1%, BKL 14.4%, MEL 11.3%, BCC 6.2%, DF 2.9%, AKIEC 2.8%, VASC 2.3%): say so when transferring tau. Never use the 193-image -E val for anything but a reported row. Preprocessing confound check (once, Session 2): for 50 official test image_ids, mean absolute pixel difference against the -E train image of the same image_id (-E train = all 10,015 HAM images sorted by id); report the number. The -C npz is NOT needed (its test set equals our CLEAN subset via the CSV); the -C benchmark proper (retrain on -C train) is an optional stretch (section 8).
2.4 Comparators with saved per-image outputs (all loaded as untrusted data: own empty directory, np.load(allow_pickle=False), shape (2005,7), rows sum to 1): Phase-2 PRIME-B run/artifacts/v2_ensemble/test_probs_tuned.npy and Phase-1/2 member probabilities (run/artifacts/single_b0, b1_112); Sanap 2026 test softmax .npy files from github.com/HrushiSanap/medmnist_ensemble_study results/dermamnist. Validation gate for Sanap's files: argmax accuracy against the official test labels must reproduce the paper's 90.57 (ViT-Base) / 90.92 (soft voting) / 91.67 (stacking) within 0.05 pt; if not, try the ISIC column order (MEL,NV,BCC,AKIEC,BKL,DF,VASC) permutation; if still not, exclude them and say so.

3. FINAL MODEL GRID (3 primary configurations x 3 seeds + 1 secondary; justified smaller than 4 x 3 because ViT-B costs ~45 GPU-min per seed and EfficientNetV2-S is the least-supported member)
Primary members (equal-weight ensemble; seeds 0 (Session 1), 1, 2):
 M1 convnext_t_224 = convnext_tiny.fb_in22k_ft_in1k (28.6 M params; 82.9 IN-1k top-1 at 224 -- cite 82.9, not 84.1 which is the 384-px checkpoint), input 224, bs 32, 30 epochs, lr 1.5e-4, wd 0.05, layer_decay 0.85 (timm create_optimizer_v2 grouping), drop_path 0.1. Measured 45 s/epoch incl. two val passes -> ~25 min/seed incl. TTA.
 M2 dinov2_b14_224 = vit_base_patch14_dinov2.lvd142m (86 M), img_size=224 (timm resamples pos_embed 37x37 -> 16x16; assert pos_embed.shape[1] == 257 and that the pretrained load reports no missing keys), bs 32, 20 epochs, lr 7e-5 (head and top block), wd 0.05, layer_decay 0.75, drop_path 0.1. Expect 55-70 img/s on a T4 -> ~45 min/seed.
 M3 densenet121_224 = densenet121.tv_in1k (8 M), 224, bs 32, 30 epochs, lr 3e-4, wd 0.02, no layer decay, no drop-path. ~24 min/seed.
Secondary single-seed members (reported, included only in the 'all-runs' ensemble rows): M4 dinov2_s14_224 = vit_small_patch14_dinov2.lvd142m, img_size 224, bs 32, 30 epochs, lr 1.5e-4, layer_decay 0.80, drop_path 0.05 (~21 min; reference arm of ablation A6). M5 effv2_s_224 (Session 1 only) = tf_efficientnetv2_s.in21k_ft_in1k, bs 32, 30 epochs, lr 2e-4, wd 0.02, layer_decay 0.80 through timm's fine-grained EfficientNet grouping (~42 depth groups: stem LR = 2e-4 x 0.8^41 ~ 2e-8, i.e. stem and early blocks effectively frozen -- disclose as 'partial fine-tuning'), drop_path 0.2, mean/std 0.5 from timm's data config. No further seeds.
Baselines: B1 base_densenet121_medmnistplus_s{0,1,2} = densenet121.ra_in1k (what timm 'densenet121' pretrained=True resolves to, as in the MedMNIST+ code) under the MedMNIST+ protocol copied line by line from github.com/sdoerrich97/rethinking-model-prototyping-MedMNISTPlus (train.py/config.yaml): no augmentation (normalise only), CE, AdamW lr 1e-4 (take weight decay exactly as their optimizer line constructs it; our reading is 1e-2), timm CosineLRScheduler t_initial=100 epochs, batch 64, max 100 epochs, early stopping on validation LOSS with patience 5, best-val-loss checkpoint evaluated once, their seeds 9930641 / 115149041 / 252139603. ~12 min/seed (stops at epoch ~10-25). Optional B1b: the same protocol with densenet121.tv_in1k, 1 seed, to pair with M3's weights. B2 frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14 linear probe + kNN-11 (probe_vit_base_patch14_dinov2, already computed in Session 1; CLS ++ mean-patch, standardised, C by val accuracy) -- guardrail: the fine-tuned M2 must beat the probe's validation top-1, otherwise the recipe is declared broken and LRs are halved, decided on validation only.
Ablation arms (seed 0): section 8.

4. RECIPE v1 (frozen = Session 1)
- Input: uint8 -> float/255 on the GPU; kornia per-sample augmentation at the training resolution S: RandomResizedCrop((S,S), scale (0.6,1.0), ratio (0.8,1.25)) -> RandomHorizontalFlip 0.5 -> RandomVerticalFlip 0.5 -> RandomAffine(degrees 180, translate 0.05, p 0.7; kornia default zero padding, so ~70% of training crops have black corners -- disclosed, frozen) -> ColorJitter(0.2, 0.2, 0.15, 0.02, p 0.8) -> RandomGaussianBlur(3x3, sigma 0.1-1.0, p 0.1) -> RandomErasing(scale 0.02-0.1, p 0.2) -> normalise with timm.data.resolve_data_config(model) mean/std.
- Batch 32 shuffled; an odd last batch is trimmed by one sample (timm Mixup asserts even batches); 219 steps/epoch (6,570 steps for 30 epochs, 4,380 for 20).
- Mixup/CutMix: timm Mixup(mixup_alpha 0.2, cutmix_alpha 1.0, prob 0.5, switch_prob 0.5, label_smoothing 0.1, num_classes 7); loss = soft-target CE on logits.float(); when mixing is off, CE with label_smoothing = cfg['ls'].
- Optimiser: timm create_optimizer_v2(opt='adamw', lr, weight_decay, layer_decay) (no decay on 1-D params by timm default); grad-norm clip 1.0; torch.autocast fp16 + GradScaler (T4 has no bf16); channels_last; cudnn.benchmark True (non-bit-reproducible; say so); no torch.compile.
- Schedule: per-step LambdaLR, linear warm-up 2 epochs from ~0, cosine to 0 at the last step.
- EMA: timm ModelEmaV3(decay 0.999, use_warmup=True), update(model, step=global_step) every step. With warm-up the decay is 1 - (1 + step)^(-2/3): 0.997 at step 6,570 and 0.994 at 4,380, so the 'final EMA' averages only the last ~1.5 epochs (0.8 for M2) of the annealed tail. Describe it in the paper as 'final weights (short-horizon EMA)'; claim no EMA benefit; the per-epoch raw-vs-EMA validation gap in history is a free diagnostic; from Session 2 also save raw-final-weight probabilities (section 5) so the raw-vs-EMA row is measured.
- Model selection: pre-registered final weights after the fixed epoch budget; no early stopping; the best-validation epoch is logged only as the 'best-epoch gap' diagnostic.
- Memory: bs 32 fits every member next to 1.5 GB of resident uint8 data (ViT-B ~6-7 GB fp16).

5. INFERENCE AND SAVED ARTEFACTS (per run directory WORK/<name>_s<seed>/, zipped and copied to Drive after every run; skip-if-done on rerun)
- TTA: the 8 dihedral views generated on the GPU (torch.rot90 k=0..3 x {identity, hflip}), autocast fp16, batch 64; store the logits of every view.
- Files: config.json (cfg, seed, torch/timm/kornia/medmnist versions, GPU name, data MD5s, script commit hash), history.json (per epoch: train loss, val top-1 raw and EMA, lr, seconds, img/s), val_logits_views.npy (1003,8,7) float32, test_logits_views.npy (2005,8,7), extE_test_logits_views.npy (1511,8,7), derived val/test/extE _tta_probs.npy (mean over views of softmax) and _clean_probs.npy (view 0), from Session 2 also test/val_tta_probs_raw.npy from the raw final weights, y_val.npy / y_test.npy / y_extE.npy, model_final_fp16.pt (Drive only, not in the zip), results.json (validation metrics, minutes, img/s; test metrics are added only by eval_phase3.py), MANIFEST.json with SHA-256 of every .npy and of the data files. Release code + probabilities + lesion map + manifest with the paper (Zenodo); the images themselves are CC BY-NC 4.0 and are not redistributed.

6. ENSEMBLE, OPERATING POINTS, CALIBRATION (every choice on validation; written to WORK/ensemble/decision_rule.json BEFORE eval_phase3.py reads any test file)
- Member probability = TTA-averaged softmax (fixed a priori; clean-view and geometric-mean variants are ablation rows).
- PRIMARY (pre-registered, no selection): for each seed s, p_ens_s = mean of {M1_s, M2_s, M3_s} with equal weights. Guardrail only: a member leaves the primary if its validation D4 top-1 is more than 2.0 pt below the best member's (expected not to fire; if it fires both compositions are reported). Three seed-matched ensembles give mean +- std (ddof=1) and the per-seed values; bootstrap CIs are given for the seed-0 ensemble and for the 9-run seed ensemble. If M2 seeds 1-2 are cut by the budget, pair M2_s0 with M1_s/M3_s and state it.
- Secondary rows (all reported): all-runs equal weight (adds M4, M5); 9-run seed ensemble; greedy forward selection on val top-1 (already in the scaffold); val-NLL-tuned simplex weights (0.1 grid); best single member; LP and kNN.
- Operating points, Phase-2 rules unchanged: score(x,k) = log p_ens(k|x) - tau * log pi_train(k), tau in {0, 0.05, ..., 1.5}. A: tau 0 (leaderboard-comparable argmax; the medmnist Evaluator uses argmax). B: largest tau whose validation top-1 is >= max - 0.005. C: argmax of validation balanced accuracy, reported with the plateau (all tau within 1 pt of the maximum) and +-0.05 sensitivity rows; validation has ~12 DF and 14 VASC images, so C is noisy by construction. Macro-AUC is invariant to tau (per-class additive constant on log-probabilities): state it. The same tau values are applied unchanged to DermaMNIST-E.
- Calibration: one ensemble-level temperature T fitted on validation by NLL; report NLL, multiclass Brier (sum over classes, mean over images), ECE with 15 equal-width bins and 15 equal-mass bins, before/after T, for p_plain (tau 0) and p_adjusted (tau_B); temperature never changes argmax, AUC or tau. Note that mixup + label smoothing make members under-confident.
- Melanoma: p(mel) as a binary score; thresholds fixed on validation (111 melanomas) for sensitivity at 80/90/95% specificity and specificity at 82/89/95% sensitivity (ISIC 2017 convention), applied to test (223 melanomas) with Wilson CIs; melanoma-vs-rest AUROC with bootstrap (and DeLong) CI and average precision; also the operating point implied by the 7-class argmax; repeated on -E (171 melanomas).

7. eval_phase3.py (CPU: numpy + sklearn + medmnist; run on Colab's CPU at the end of each session; the Mac runs only the numpy-only aggregate_phase3.py)
- Official ACC/AUC through medmnist.Evaluator('dermamnist', 'test', size=224, root='/content').evaluate(p) (labels are read from root/dermamnist_224.npz; assert p.shape == (2005, 7) because the Evaluator checks rows only); sklearn balanced_accuracy_score, f1_score(average='macro'), top-3; per-class recall/specificity/precision/F1 with Wilson CIs and OvR AUC with bootstrap CI; 7x7 confusion counts for A/B/C.
- Uncertainty: percentile bootstrap over test images, B = 10,000 for ACC/balanced/F1 and 2,000 for AUC, fixed RNG seed, identical resample indices for all systems (paired differences); PLUS a lesion-cluster bootstrap (resample lesion_ids with replacement via the map of 2.2). Seed std and bootstrap CI in separate columns, never conflated.
- Paired significance (McNemar: exact binomial if b + c < 25 else mid-p; report b, c, p, paired delta-ACC with bootstrap CI; Holm-Bonferroni across baselines, uncorrected p also shown): primary ensemble vs Phase-2 PRIME-B; vs Phase-1 B0@96 and the B1@112 member; vs our DenseNet-121 MedMNIST+ reproduction (seed-matched); vs each single member; vs Sanap's ViT-B / soft-voting / stacking outputs if they pass the gate in 2.4.
- Lesion decomposition: every system's top-1, balanced, macro-AUC on CLEAN (1,227) and LEAKED (778) with CIs, including PRIME-B and Sanap's outputs -- the paper's central table and figure. Also subgroup rows the metadata allows (dx_type, source dataset, sex, age band).
- DermaMNIST-E: ACC/AUC (MedMNIST definitions), balanced, F1 at tau_A/B/C for every member and ensemble; the reference row Abhishek et al. ResNet-18@224 0.685 / 0.896 was trained on all 10,015 HAM images (43% more data) -- say so; ISIC-2018 leaderboard and reader-study numbers only if re-confirmed.
- Model-selection accounting: print the number of validation-selected scalars (tau_B, tau_C, T, optional weights) and the fact that the validation split shares 113 lesions with test.
- Figures: validation curves (raw vs EMA) per member; tau trade-off (validation solid, test dashed and labelled 'not used for selection'); confusion matrices A/B/C; per-class recall; reliability diagram; CLEAN-vs-LEAKED bars for ours / PRIME-B / Sanap / plain-recipe arm; official-vs-E scatter per system.

8. ABLATIONS (seed 0; reference arm = the frozen recipe v1 run; cost; priority)
 A1 Recipe / memorisation ladder on ConvNeXt-T (MUST): (a) abl_convnext_t_plain: aug 'none' (normalise only), mixup/cutmix off, label smoothing 0, drop_path 0, same AdamW/LLRD/cosine/30 epochs/EMA; save BOTH final-EMA probabilities and the best-validation-accuracy-checkpoint probabilities (Sanap-style selection, labelled validation-selected). (b) abl_convnext_t_nomix: full augmentation + LS 0.1 + drop-path, mixup/cutmix off (session2_configs.json entry). (c) full = M1_s0. Evaluate on full / CLEAN / LEAKED / -E. Pre-registered reading: if plain >= full on the official split but full >= plain on CLEAN or -E, the recipe is a robustness gain, not an accuracy gain; report whatever sign appears. ~22 + 25 min.
